```{r libraries}
# devtools::install("../fridge") #run this in console
library(fridge)
library(ggelato)
library(fabletools)
library(feasts)
library(tsibble)
library(dplyr)
load("../data/tourism_new.rda")
```

## Data

Australian Domestic Tourism data in `tsibble` package is used in this example. First, we need to aggregate the data by its hierarchical structure `(State/Region)*Purpose` using `fabletools::aggregate_key()`. This means that `Region` is nested within `State` and `Purpose` has crossed relationships with both of `State` and `Region`.

```{r echo = FALSE}
# tourism_hts <- bind_rows(tsibble::tourism, tourism_new) |>
#   mutate(
#     Region = recode(
#       Region,
#       "Experience Perth" = "Destination Perth",
#       "Launceston, Tamar and the North" = "Launceston and the North",
#       "Wilderness West" = "West Coast",
#       "Northern" = "Townsville",
#       "Outback" = "Outback Queensland",
#       "Darling Downs" = "Queensland Country",
#       "Kakadu Arnhem" = "Litchfield Kakadu Arnhem",
#       "Murraylands" = "Murray River, Lakes and Coorong"
#     )
#   ) |> aggregate_key((State / Region) * Purpose, Trips = sum(Trips))

```


```{r data}
new_name <- c(
  "Experience Perth"                = "Destination Perth",
  "Launceston, Tamar and the North" = "Launceston and the North",
  "Wilderness West"                 = "West Coast",
  "Northern"                        = "Townsville",
  "Outback"                         = "Outback Queensland",
  "Kakadu Arnhem"                   = "Litchfield Kakadu Arnhem",
  "Murraylands"                     = "Murray River, Lakes and Coorong",
  "Melbourne East"                  = "Yarra Valley and Dandenong Ranges",
  "Upper Yarra"                     = "Yarra Valley and Dandenong Ranges",
  "Darling Downs"                   = "Central Queensland")   # pooled, split below

split_to <- c("Capricorn Coast", "Gladstone", "Queensland Country")

# Update region names
tourism_full <- bind_rows(tsibble::tourism, tourism_new) |> as_tibble() |>
  mutate(Region = recode(Region, !!!new_name)) |>
  summarise(Trips = sum(Trips), .by = c(Quarter, State, Region, Purpose))

# Share of each new region in 2018-2022, by purpose
region_share <- filter(tourism_full, Region %in% split_to) |>
  summarise(p = sum(Trips), .by = c(Region, Purpose)) |> mutate(p = p / sum(p), .by = Purpose)

# Split the pooled old series with those shares
tourism_split <- filter(tourism_full, Region == "Central Queensland") |> select(-Region) |>
  inner_join(region_share, by = "Purpose", relationship = "many-to-many") |> mutate(Trips = Trips * p, p = NULL)

tourism_hts <- bind_rows(filter(tourism_full, Region != "Central Queensland"), tourism_split) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Quarter, key = c(State, Region, Purpose)) |>
  aggregate_key((State / Region) * Purpose, Trips = sum(Trips))

# tourism_hts <- tsibble::tourism |> 
#   aggregate_key((State / Region) * Purpose, Trips = sum(Trips))
```

## Time series features plot

```{r hts features}
tourism_ft <- tourism_hts |>
  features(Trips, feature_set(pkgs = "feasts"))

tourism_feasts <- gig(tourism_ft,
    gig_aes(x = trend_strength, 
            y = seasonal_strength_year),
    structure = (State/Region)*Purpose) +
  geom_features()

tourism_feasts

```

## STL decomposition plot

```{r reuse-2}
stl_original <- tourism_hts |>
  model(stl = STL(Trips)) |>
  components()

stl_scaled <- tourism_hts |>
  group_by_key() |>
  mutate(Trips = as.numeric(scale(Trips))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  model(stl = STL(Trips)) |>
  components()

tourism_stl <- gig(
  stl_original,
  gig_aes(
    x = Quarter,
    y = Trips,
    seasonality = season_year,
    trend = trend,
    remainder = remainder
  ),
  structure = (State / Region) * Purpose
) +
  geom_stl(scaled = stl_scaled)

tourism_stl
```

## Sunburst

```{r sunburst}
tourism_sunburst <- gig(tourism_hts, 
    structure = (State/Region)*Purpose) +
  geom_sunburst(labels = TRUE) 

tourism_sunburst
```

## Coordinating multiple plots with `fridge()` in `fridge` `R` package

:::{.column-screen}
```{r}
fridge(tourism_stl,
       tourism_feasts, 
       tourism_sunburst, 
       fullscreen = FALSE) 
```

:::
